From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Order Form — IP carveouts & feedback license (Cardinal Systems)

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Cardinal sent an updated order form with IP redlines attached (Cardinal_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.pdf). Key asks from them:
- They want an explicit "no-training" carveout for customer data used with our hosted API (they propose a permanent opt-out).
- A feedback license: Cardinal requests that any feedback they provide during the pilot be owned by them and excluded from our productization path.
- Output ownership: they asked for assignment of output for the specific Product modules they deploy.

My read: the output assignment ask is narrow (product modules only) but the training opt-out + ownership of feedback together create a big operational gap for our model improvement pipeline and for downstream productization. We need a single position we can defend operationally and legally.

Questions for legal/ops alignment before I reply:
1) Can we accept a time-limited training opt-out (e.g., 18 months) instead of permanent?
2) If we grant a feedback license carveout, can we retain telemetry/anonymous signal for model quality measurement?
3) Will assigning output for defined modules require changes to our standard MSA/Order Form templates (procurement asks)?

Proposed next steps:
- Ben: short legal playbook bullets we can send back to Sasha today.
- Marissa: draft a tracked clause that offers an 18-month opt-out + audit log commitment instead of full assignment.
- I will propose an internal exec exception path if Cardinal insists on permanent assignment.

Attached: Cardinal_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.pdf (redline), redline_summary.xlsx (internal summary).

Thanks,
Irene
--

Irene — quick thoughts:
- Output assignment: narrow assignment tied to specific modules is ok only if we maintain an explicit exclusion for any models/weights/derivative model artifacts. In short: they can own the generated output (UI text, documents) for those modules, but not model artifacts or rights to retrain our models.
- Training opt-out: permanent opt-out is non-starter. We should offer a limited opt-out (12–24 months) with the ability to opt back in after an agreed notice period.
- Feedback license: we can accept a customer-only feedback license for product feedback (bug reports, feature suggestions) but we must retain the right to include anonymized telemetry for quality improvement.

If Cardinal pushes hard on permanent training prohibition, escalate to Risk/Exec. We can offer enhanced audit logs + data retention guarantees as compromise.

I'll draft 3 bullets and loop in Legal counsel if needed.

—Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — IP carveouts & feedback license (Cardinal Systems)

Folks — attaching a suggested clause (proposed_orderform_clause.docx) that tries to balance Cardinal's asks with our operational needs. High-level approach:
- Output: provide a narrow assignment for "Customer-Generated Output" defined as the literal outputs produced by the Product for the Customer's input. Explicitly exclude model weights, training datasets, and aggregated telemetry.
- Training: offer an 18-month opt-out window from go-live. During that window we will:
  * Not use Customer data to train our production models;
  * Retain anonymized signals for quality metrics (no PII, aggregated);
  * Permit an independent audit on the retention/audit controls once during the opt-out period.
- Feedback: accept customer ownership of feedback they provide as part of the pilot, but include a limited, non-exclusive license back to Redwood to use that feedback to fix/operate the service (bug fixes, stability), and a time-limited right (24 months) to use anonymized, aggregated signals for model improvement.

If Cardinal wants permanent assignment or to block anonymized telemetry, we should either:
- Require premium fee / enterprise carveout (Reserved capacity pricing), or
- Route to procurement + legal for exec exception.

Marked-up language highlights are in the doc. I recommend we send this version to Sasha with clear callouts and ask for a 48-hour review cycle.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Legal — Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_orderform_clause.docx

Irene / team — thanks for the quick follow-up and for the proposed language. Cardinal is aligned on most of the suggested edits and appreciates the limited-scope approach to output assignment. A few points from our side:

- Training opt-out: Cardinal's position remains that customer data processed through hosted APIs should not be used to improve third-party models unless we sign an explicit consent. Our preference is permanent opt-out; however, we can consider 18 months if Redwood can commit to strong technical controls and an audit window.

- Audit logs: we will accept the 18-month proposal only if Redwood provides immutable audit logs (readable) for the first 12 months and a third-party attestation at the 12-month mark.

- Feedback: Cardinal will provide feedback during the engagement and wants ownership of that feedback for their internal productization. We are willing to grant Redwood a limited, non-exclusive right to use feedback for operational fixes and to anonymize signals for quality improvements for a finite period only if we get an express opt-in in the master services schedule.

Next steps from our side:
1) We will review the proposed_orderform_clause.docx and produce marginal comments by EOD Monday (Nov 8).
2) Cardinal legal will also need a short call with Redwood to walk through the audit log technical approach — can your infra/ops lead join?
